title: Mexico at the World Cup
description: El Tri, the Azteca, and the infamous Quinto Partido — test your knowledge of Mexico's World Cup history.

questions.q: What is Mexico's best ever World Cup result?
questions.explain: Mexico reached the quarter-finals twice — in 1970 and 1986, both times as hosts. They were eliminated 4–1 by Italy in 1970 and on penalties by West Germany in 1986.

questions.q: Mexico has hosted the World Cup in 1970 and in which other year?
questions.explain: Mexico hosted the 1986 World Cup after Colombia withdrew. It produced some of the tournament's greatest moments, including Maradona's 'Hand of God' and 'Goal of the Century'.

questions.q: How many consecutive Round of 16 exits did Mexico suffer between 1994 and 2018?
questions.explain: Mexico were eliminated in the Round of 16 in 1994, 1998, 2002, 2006, 2010, 2014 and 2018 — seven straight tournaments, a run known as the 'Quinto Partido' (fifth match) curse.

questions.q: Who is Mexico's all-time top scorer at World Cups?
questions.explain: Javier 'Chicharito' Hernandez scored 4 World Cup goals — 1 in 2010 against Argentina, and 3 in 2014 including a brace against Croatia.

questions.q: Hirving 'Chucky' Lozano scored the winner as Mexico famously beat which team 1–0 at the 2018 World Cup?
questions.explain: Mexico beat reigning champions Germany 1–0 in their opening game at Russia 2018. Lozano's 35th-minute strike caused wild celebrations in Mexico City — literally an earthquake.

questions.q: Mexico was controversially eliminated from the 2022 World Cup group stage despite beating Saudi Arabia. Why?
options: They were eliminated on fair play
questions.explain: Mexico beat Saudi Arabia 2–1 but needed a 3-goal win to progress. Poland, who drew 0–0 with Argentina, advanced ahead of Mexico on goal difference.

questions.q: Diego Maradona's 'Hand of God' and 'Goal of the Century' against England in 1986 were scored at which Mexican stadium?
questions.explain: Both goals were scored at the Estadio Azteca in Mexico City during the 1986 quarter-final, in what is widely regarded as the greatest individual performance in World Cup history.

questions.q: What is Mexico's famous national stadium, which hosted two World Cup finals (1970 and 1986)?
questions.explain: The Estadio Azteca in Mexico City is the only stadium to host two World Cup finals — Brazil vs Italy in 1970 and Argentina vs West Germany in 1986.

questions.q: USA fans coined the term 'Dos a Cero' for their rivalry with Mexico. What does it refer to?
options: Mexico often beat USA by that score
USA repeatedly beat Mexico 2–0 in qualifying
The first World Cup match between them ended 2–0
questions.explain: 'Dos a Cero' (two to zero) became a running joke after the USA beat Mexico by that exact scoreline in four consecutive World Cup qualifying matches at home between 2001 and 2013.

questions.q: Mexico's nickname is 'El Tri'. What does this refer to?
options: The three biggest cities in Mexico
The three greatest players in Mexican history
The three colours of the Mexican flag
The three times they reached the quarter-finals
questions.explain: El Tri (short for El Tricolor) refers to the three colours of the Mexican flag — green, white and red.
